q: What ESG rating products must a SEBI-registered ESG rating provider offer?
title: ESG rating products SEBI requires
short: SEBI requires every registered ESG rating provider to offer at least six products: an ESG rating, a Transition or Parivartan score, a Combined score, and Core versions of all three built only on assured data. All ratings use a 0 to 100 scale, must be comparable across sectors and must reflect Indian context.
audience: Listed companies, investors and suppliers asked about ESG scores

ol: Combined score, joining the ESG rating and the transition score.
Core ESG rating, based only on third-party assured or audited data.

sections.h: Rules that apply to all six
ul: Scores run from 0 to 100, where 100 is the best.
Each product needs a distinct name, prefix or suffix so users can tell them apart.
Ratings must be sector-agnostic so companies in different sectors can be compared.
They must reflect environmental, social and governance aspects that matter in India; SEBI gives an indicative list of Indian parameters.

p: If a provider's ESG rating already uses only assured data, it need not issue a separate Core version. If transition assessment is built into the ESG rating, it need not offer a separate Combined score. In both cases the provider must say so in its rationale and methodology.

sections.h: What legally counts as an ESG rating
p: The CRA Regulations define ESG ratings broadly: any rating product marketed as an opinion on an issuer's or security's ESG profile, exposure to ESG, climate or environmental risk, or impact on society and the environment, issued using a ranking system, whether or not it is called an ESG rating. Since 4 July 2023 these providers are regulated under the CRA Regulations.

senseible: Senseible is not an ESG rating provider. For a supplier, its bill-based energy and emissions records are the kind of evidence a listed buyer uses when its own ESG rating is assessed.
